title: centaurea montana subsp. variegata
intro: Centaurea montana subsp. variegata, commonly known as Mountain Cornflower, is a flowering plant species within the daisy family (Asteraceae) known for its vibrant blue and white variegated flowers. The plant has been traditionally used in herbal medicine due to its potential health benefits, including reducing inflammation, soothing digestive issues, and exhibiting antimicrobial properties. The therapeutic actions of Mountain Cornflower are attributed to its bioactive constituents, which include flavonoids, saponins, and phenolic acids, that may help to modulate the immune system and alleviate oxidative stress. The plant's bioactive compounds have also been studied for their potential to exhibit antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antiviral effects.
